key_insight: Natural-image pretraining improved medical diffusion generation, with benefits linked to spatial structure rather than semantics.
clinical_relevance: Better synthetic-image fidelity may support medical imaging research, but the reported proxy improvements do not establish clinical utility or safety.
method: Compared natural-image initialization with training from scratch and alternative pretraining or reinitialization schemes.
Evaluated pixel- and latent-space diffusion models spanning 131M–952M parameters.
Probed internal representations and tested mixed natural–medical image training.
evidence_signal: Across RadImageNet and BraTS, natural-image initialization improved relative gFID by 21–34% in pixel space and 14% in latent space, with gains mirrored by pathology-classification and radiomic-feature evaluations.
watch_item: Results cover two radiology datasets and proxy fidelity measures; generalization to other settings and clinical use remains unestablished.
paper_title: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation
